course_title: Music on Screen: Movies, TV and Games
course_description:
This course is an historical overview of musical accompaniment in film and television and provides access to theoretical frameworks that have evolved within the emerging field of film and television music studies.

Students will gain a greater appreciation of film, television and video game music and the broader implications of music on screen as the course investigates the following key issues: the industrial and cultural place of the film and television score, the film musical, the soundtrack album, and the pop music television program; music as support to film action, narrative, and emotional affect; music as cultural, ethnic or period marker; music as a locus for gender, race or youth audience identification.

The course draws on film music theories that accommodate both scored and compilation soundtrack films, investigates television scoring, examines the emergence of pop music television programming and the rise of music video and video games, and reflects on the significant commercial and formal influence that film and music have had on each other since the 1920s.

assessment_details.title: Minor Essay
assessment_details.task_description: Write a close textual analysis of a brief (approx. five minutes) music sequence from a film or television programme of your choice. The essay should take the form of an examination of the narrative relationship between music and image in your chosen clip, and highlight pertinent theoretical or industrial connections relevant to the course, placing the chosen sequence within a researched scholarly framework. A detailed criteria sheet will be available in the Blackboard Assessment section. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Major Essay
assessment_details.task_description: Present a focused theoretical research essay based on one of the following topics: · silent film accompaniment · the introduction of film sound · industrial and cultural implications of the classical Hollywood score · music and film genre · alternatives to the classical score · jazz and film · art film or world cinema scores · rock movies since the 1950s · the rock compilation score · music documentary · film music and the auteur director · the film musical · video game music · the online relationship of music and visuals Your essay should demonstrate an ability to define and research relevant and specific areas of film music studies. Research should take into account existing scholarly studies of the interrelations between music and visual media, and attempt to place representative texts within an established scholarly framework. Detailed analyses of selected aspects of musical soundtracks from specific films, television programs or games should be provided where appropriate in order to illustrate the relationship between music and image, or highlight pertinent theoretical or industrial connections. A detailed criteria sheet will be available in the Blackboard Assessment section. Read full task description Hide full task description
